contract.completion: All three milestones and all final cumulative visible and hidden cases pass at exact release commit
contract.intermediate_hidden: Retrospective diagnostic; earlier defects may be repaired
contract.interruption: Settled controller exit after milestone two, new PID resumes exact Git checkpoint
contract.scope: Bounded stateless patch workers with persistent controller; no gossip transport comparison

hypotheses: A reviewed cheap-model portfolio may reduce final requirement omissions compared with a sequential cheap-model agent.
A strong single-model agent may match or exceed the portfolio; no superiority is assumed.
Controller persistence may improve completion while masking premature agent completion; count both separately.
interpretation: 12 synthetic project trajectories are a pilot, not statistical evidence of general superiority.
The portfolio bundles diversity, reviewer strength, and additional calls; effects cannot be attributed separately.
Only sequential process persistence and explicit legacy migration are tested, not database contention or recovery from a process crash.
A completed milestone uses visible checks; only the final release uses private checks.
Earlier hidden defects fixed later are permitted; intermediate private scores are diagnostic.
Cost and wall time are secondary measurements and safety guardrails; their long-term improvement is unproven.
primary_question: Does the system complete the full cumulative project at the required quality bar, preserve earlier behavior, and continue through failures and a settled controller restart?
